summary: The Xianix Agent delivers a multi-tenant control plane that turns platform webhooks into isolated Claude Code executions, plus an executor image and an AI-DLC lifecycle service built on label-driven agents. Planning is documented in depth: architecture objectives, a tenant-isolation design, a rules specification, a webhook guide, an AI-DLC process with explicit human review gates, and Azure infrastructure and deployment runbooks. Controls are strong for the executor: shellcheck and a hermetic integration-test tier gate every tagged publish. They're weak for the agent image, which publishes on tag without running its 150 unit tests. Most commits reach `main` without a pull request, releases have no notes, and deployment always pulls `:latest`. Some maintained documents no longer match the code. There's no incident or rollback procedure. No core obligation is a Gap, so the overall 8.1 status is Partial.
